headline: KSE-100 gives back the week's rebound, sliding 1.30% to 175,802.78 as a surprise current-account deficit and a maxed-out conflict gauge push the desk toward banks, E&P and fertilizer.
summary: Friday's 1.30% drop to 175,802.78 erased most of the week's Hormuz-selloff rebound after Pakistan's current account swung to a roughly $650m deficit in June, tipping the full FY26 external account into deficit versus last year's surplus. On top of that, Brent near $86, a jumpy VIX and a 6.7% weekly drop in SBP reserves keep the backdrop tense, with conflict-escalation stress on the desk's geo-risk radar pinned at its maximum reading over the Iran-Hormuz standoff. The desk is leaning cautious: banks, E&P and fertilizer screen best on rate carry, oil realizations and domestic demand, while OMCs, cement, autos and textile exporters carry the FX and import-cost risk. New setups stay capped at two names until the picture clears.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Policy rate is still 11.5% and T-bill funding costs are sub-policy-rate, supportive for bank margins even though Commercial Banks was the single biggest index drag today (-680 points) on the current-account news.

sectors.name: E&P (Oil & Gas Exploration)
sectors.why: Brent near $86 on the Hormuz standoff is a direct tailwind for realized crude/gas prices, though the sector still shed 327 index points today on broader profit-taking.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Domestic-demand businesses with low direct oil-import exposure — a relative safe harbour while the import bill and current account are under pressure.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: A weaker external-account backdrop plus fuel-price/margin and circular-debt risk make OMCs the wrong place to carry FX exposure right now.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-cost sensitive and among today's sharper decliners (-266 index points) on the same current-account read.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: Imported-input costs and a still-fragile rupee squeeze margins even as FY26 unit sales rose 39% — the cost side, not demand, is the near-term risk.

sectors.name: Textiles / Exporters
sectors.why: FY26 textile exports were effectively flat YoY and June alone fell 16.7% YoY — the export-slowdown side of the current-account swing, plus Hormuz shipping-route risk.

watchlist.angle: The desk's top predictability score on the board (75.7/100) and three separate proven strategies on its own price history — consolidation-break has hit 85% of the time over 13 trades (100% out-of-sample) — plus a real, confirmed catalyst: a 6.6% final dividend with book closure 25-27 July 2026. Low beta (-0.04) also fits a risk-off tilt toward income names.
watchlist.risk: P/E is already elevated (16.64x) and the payout ratio is a stretched 106% — a soft year could force a dividend cut, and buying right before book closure means paying up for the payout.

watchlist.angle: Banks are one of the regime's three favoured sectors, and UBL's consolidation-break strategy has worked 76% of the time on its own history (net +2.2%/trade, still 80% out-of-sample). Fundamentals back it up — fair P/E, a 30% net margin, and a covered 6.81% dividend (56% payout). Q2 results are pencilled for 2026-07-22, a live near-term catalyst.
watchlist.risk: The results date is an unconfirmed scraped estimate, and banks were today's single biggest index drag (-680 points) on the current-account news — a weak print here would confirm that move.

watchlist.angle: Fertilizer is a favoured sector this regime, and FFC's 52-week-high breakout is the best-performing proven strategy on its own history — 78% hit rate, +3.17% net expectancy, still 71% out-of-sample. Forward P/E (6.89) sits below trailing (9.22), implying expected earnings growth, plus a 6.71% yield. Results are pencilled for 2026-07-29.
watchlist.risk: The breakout trigger hasn't actually fired — the stock closed today below its 20-day average and 5.3% off its recent high, so this is a watch-list name, not a live signal.

watchlist.angle: Banks favoured; HBL is one of the cheapest large-cap names on the desk (P/E 6.85) with a well-covered 7.76% yield (40% payout) and price holding above both its 20- and 50-day averages. Its own history shows a working oscillator setup (Stochastic reclaim 50: 63% hit rate).
watchlist.risk: The technical edge here is thin (net expectancy under 1%) and results are more than three weeks out (2026-08-11, unconfirmed) — this is a fundamentals-led watch more than an active trigger.

catalysts.event: DCR book closure begins (confirmed 6.6% final dividend)
SBP MPC — first monetary policy decision of FY27
PBS July CPI release — first print to capture this month's fuel-price hikes and the Hormuz oil spike

risks: The US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz standoff is unresolved — any fresh escalation reprices oil and PKR risk again, as it did twice already this month.

SBP reserves are down 6.7% WoW on debt repayments and the current account has swung to deficit; a further external-account slip would pressure the rupee and could turn the SBP more hawkish, undermining the bank-carry thesis.
Earnings season is starting (UBL, FFC, banks through August) — a disappointing print in a favoured sector would confirm rather than reverse today's selling.
